currentEditorialSignals.title: Dog-Essential Points Along the Route
currentEditorialSignals.signal: AllTrails added more than 500,000 mapped viewpoints, landmarks and trail amenities in 2025. Strava made POIs tappable, added contextual details and enabled routing directly to or through them.
currentEditorialSignals.ormaOpportunity: Define a tightly governed dog-essential POI model: reliable water, shade or rest areas, livestock encounters, leash-transition points, gates, emergency exits, dog-permitted transport, nearby vets and places where water should not be assumed. Attach each item to its route position and evidence status.
currentEditorialSignals.whyNow: Competitors are making POIs actionable, but generic amenity catalogues rarely explain their canine relevance or reliability.
suggestedInvestigation: Which POI types materially change a guardian’s decision?
Which require authoritative evidence versus editorial observation?
How should seasonal or unreliable water be represented?
Should POIs appear on the elevation profile as well as the map?
Which POIs belong in trail verification versus ongoing hazard monitoring?

currentEditorialSignals.title: Decision-Point Route Narrative
currentEditorialSignals.signal: onX positions expert-built routes around explicit decision points and terrain insight, while Strava’s redesigned recording experience keeps the map and key statistics visible together instead of forcing screen switching.
currentEditorialSignals.ormaOpportunity: Turn ORMA’s verified route-order and trail-number evidence into a concise, location-aware narrative: upcoming junction, outgoing and incoming trail reference, landmark, distance from start and dog-specific action. The same structured content could support the trail page, navigation and offline pack.
currentEditorialSignals.whyNow: ORMA’s operating standard already requires unusually rigorous evidence for route direction and trail-number changes. Productizing that structure could create a defensible clarity advantage without generating new claims.
suggestedInvestigation: Can existing dossiers consistently produce structured decision points?
Which junctions deserve proactive guidance rather than passive map labels?
How should dog actions such as “lead on” be distinguished from navigation instructions?
What is the fallback when a sign, path or reference cannot be verified?
Can one editorial structure serve web, mobile and offline contexts without duplication?
